text: The assembly will now hear an address by
His Highness Shik Sabah Al Khaled
Alhammed al-Mubarak al- Sabah, Crown
Prince of the State of Q8. I request
protocol to accompany his highness. I
invite him to address the assembly.
Thank you, Mr. President. In the name of
God, most compassionate, most merciful,
your excellency, President of the
General Assembly, your Excellency,
Secretary General, Your Majesties,
Excellencies, Highnesses, ladies and
gentlemen, may the peace and blessings
of God be upon you. At the outset, I am
pleased to convey to you the greetings
of his highness, the amir of the state
of Kuwait, Sheikh Mal al Ahmed al Jabir
al- Sabah.
Along with his wishes for the success of
this session, we would also like to
congratulate his excellency Dr. Khalil
Rahman and the friendly people People
People's Republic of Bangladesh on his
election as president of the General
Assembly. We affirm our support for his
excellency and we salute his wise choice
of theme for this session. Restoring
trust and managing transformation, a
united nations
that delivers for all. We would also
like to express our gratitude to her
excellency Miss Analina Berboka for her
valued efforts during her presidency of
the previous session. We would be remiss
not to applaud the efforts, good offices
and initiatives of the secretary general
aimed at strengthening multilateralism
and that include initiatives such as
UN80
and the pact for the future as well as
the ongoing efforts to address global
challenges, crisis, conflicts, wars,
climate change and terrorism as well as
the efforts to assist member states in
order to achieve these sustainable
development goals and to strengthen
international cooperation on artificial
ele intelligence. We hope that these
efforts will continue beyond the
conclusion of the secretary general's
term in an in a manner to guarantee the
continuity of work to reform and develop
the organization's body's
enhance its effectiveness and
performance in discharging its
responsibilities. In this context, we
emphasize that security council reform
and the security council is the body
charged with maintaining international
peace and security has become essential
to keep pace with the significant
increase in the number of member states
and the changes in international
relations since the establishment of the
organization.
There is an urgent need for the council
to become more representative,
effective, and transparent in carrying
out its responsibilities.
Mr. President, uh, since last February,
the state of Kuwait, the countries of
the Gulf Cooperation Council and the
Hashite Kingdom of Jordan have been
subjected to illegal Iranian aggression
involving ballistic ballistic missiles,
cruise missiles, and drones.
All while we are not a party to the
conflict in the region. These attacks
are a flagrant violation of the
international law, international
humanitarian law and the UN charter.
These brutal attacks have systematically
and repeatedly targeted civilian objects
and critical infrastructure,
including Kuwait International Airport,
power and water stations, oil facilities
as well, revealing a hostile approach
aimed at disrupting the foundations of
life and critical infrastructure.
These heinous attacks have claimed the
lives of several martyrs and innocent
civilians. They have also resulted in
numerous injuries and have inflicted
material and economic damage.
And furthermore, to inflict harm on the
economies of the region and the world
and to disrupt global trade and oil
markets, Iran is obstructing maritime
navigation and closing the strait of
Hormuz to use it as a bargaining chip in
the war in violation of international
law and the relevant security council
resolutions.
In this regard, the state of Kuwait
expresses its deep appreciation to the
brotherly and friendly nations who have
stood by Kuwait and demonstrated
solidarity. We also salute the countries
that have sponsored Security Council
resolution 2817 and other resolutions
issued by the Human Rights Council and
the International Maritime Organization,
which have condemned the Iranian
aggression as a threat to international
peace and security.
demanding its cessation and affirming
the inherent rights of states to
self-defense as per article 51 of the UN
charter. They have also stressed the
importance of guaranteeing freedom of
navigation without restrictions or
conditions and based on
Kuwait's belief that the security and
stability of the Arabian Gulf region
constitutes a fundamental pillar of
regional and international security and
stability as demonstrated by the
repercussions of the war and Iranian
aggressions.
We reiterate the support for all
diplomatic efforts aimed at deescalation
and a peaceful resolution to the
existing dispute.
And we applaud the mediation efforts led
by Qatar and Pakistan while emphasizing
the need to reach a sustainable regional
understanding based on a firm commitment
to the principles of good
neighborliness, respect for state
sovereignty and a non-interference in
internal affairs as well as refraining
from the use or threat uh of use of
force.
In addition to seizing support for
proxies and militias and addressing the
security concerns of all countries in
the region, including
the Iranian nuclear file, ballistic
missiles and drones while stressing the
guarantee of freedom and safety of
navigation and the right of passage
through the straits of Hormuz and Babel
Mandab in accordance with the
international law and the 1982 UN
convention on law of the sea. Mr.
President, the state of Kuwait is
committed in its foreign policy to the
principles of the UN charter, in
particular, respect for the principle of
good neighborliness, respect for state
sovereignty, and the non-inference in
internal affairs.
Accordingly, the state of Kuwait views
the brotherly Republic of Iraq as a
neighbor with whom we share close ties
as a and are partners in security and
stability since the fall of the former
regime in 2003. Kuwait has supported and
stood by Iraq fa in facing security,
political and economic challenges in
order to help Iraq restore its regional
and international role in standing.
Kuwait believes that a stable, secure,
and prosperous Iraq serves the shared
interests of Kuwait and the entire
region. In this context, the state of
Kuwait commends the measures taken by
the Iraqi Prime Minister, Mr. Ali Alzi,
to consolidate arms under state control
and to strengthen Iraq's bilateral
relations with neighboring countries.
We look forward to enhancing confidence
building measures between the two
countries and to elevate our bilateral
relations to broader horizons as well as
to resolve all outstanding issues. Most
important of these issues are the
maritime border demarcation beyond
marker 162 as per the rules of
international law and the 1982 UN
convention on law of the sea.
We also emphasize the need to adhere to
bilateral security and technical
agreements and arrangements signed
between the two countries.
Very important among these agreements
is the Abdullah
uh agreement and the 2008 security
exchange protocol. These agreements
serve as vital legal and practical
instruments for regulating navigation,
protecting the environment, combating
terrorism, as well as combating the
illicit trafficking of arms and
narcotics, and enhancing shared
security. The state of quit calls upon
Iraq to cooperate with the high level
representative of the secretary general
pursuant to security council resolution
2792 in order to achieve the progress
and desired outcomes regarding
Kuwaiti prisoners and missing persons as
well as nationals of third countries and
the recovery of Kuwaiti property
including the national archives. Mr. Mr.
President, the state of Kuwait
reiterates its principled and firm
position condemning the ongoing
violations by the Israeli occupation
forces against the brotherly Palestinian
people. The Palestinian people continue
to suffer under difficult living
conditions caused by policies of
displacement, arrests, and settlement.
We call for the full implementation of
the comprehensive peace plan and its sub
subsequent phase adopted by security
council resolution 2803.
This includes the complete withdrawal of
Israeli occupation forces from Gaza, the
assurance of humanitarian aid access
and the return of the Palestinian
Authority to the Gaza Strip. We affirm
that the Gaza Strip is an integral part
of the occupied Palestinian territory.
In this regard, we welcome the measures
and decisions taken by the United
Kingdom, France, and several other
nations to condemn settlement activities
and to impose sanctions against settlers
involved in acts of violence and
terrorism against Palestinians
as well as banning the import of goods
and products originating from the
settlements.
The state of Kuwait reiterates that a
just, comprehensive, and lasting peace
in the region remains contingent upon an
end to the Israeli occupation of all
Arab territories, as well as enabling
the Palestinian people to exercise their
legitimate and inalienable rights.
It also rests upon the establishment of
an independent Palestinian state on the
borders of June 4th, 1967 with East
Jerusalem as its capital.
Mr. President, the sisterly Republic of
Yemen is witnessing a serious military
escalation as a result of the attacks by
Houthi militias against several
governorates and areas along the west
coast aimed at threatening navigation in
the Babel Mandab Strait. In this regard,
the state of Kuwait reiterated its full
support for UN-led efforts aimed at a
comprehensive, sustainable and Yemenled
settlement in accordance with the three
agreed references
and the relevant security council
resolutions, in particular resolution
The state of Kuwait affirms that any
political settlement must safeguard
Yemen's unity, sovereignty,
independence, and territorial integrity.
A settlement must end the suffering of
the Yemeni people and must open
prospects for security, stability, and
economic development. We also stress the
need to preserve the security and safety
of maritime navigation in the Red Sea
and the Babel Mandabub Strait.
We also condemn in the strongest terms
the attacks by the Houthis against the
sisterly kingdom of Saudi Arabia
targeting civilian and economic
facilities in several cities. In this
context, we affirm that the security of
the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is an
integral part of the security of the
state of Kuwait and the security of the
GCC states. Mr. Mr. President, the state
of Kuwait reiterates its solidarity with
the sisterly Syrian Arab Republic. We
welcome the measures taken by the
international community to lift the
sanctions against Syria and to remove
Syria's name from the list of state
sponsors of terrorism. We also affirm
our support for all efforts aimed at
rebuilding state institutions and aimed
at advancing a Syrian-led comprehensive
inclusive political process
led by the Syrians with the active
participation of all segments of society
in Syria and aimed at fulfilling their
aspirations for security, stability, and
a life of dignity. In this context, we
stress the need to respect Syria's
sovereignty, unity, and territorial
integrity.
We condemn and reject the attacks and
incursions by Israeli occupation forces
into Syrian territory.
These acts are a serious escalation and
a violation of the 1974 disengagement of
forces agreement. They undermine
security and stability in the region.
With regards to the sisterly Lebanese
Republic, the state of Kuwait affirms
the importance of Lebanese state
institutions and the need to extend
their full authority over the entire
territory of Lebanon and to restrict the
possession of arms exclusively to the
state, thereby reinforcing Lebanon's
sovereignty and preserving its security
and stability. Here we also emphasize
the importance of maintaining an
international presence along the blue
line to ensure the full implementation
of UN resolution 1701. And we reiterate
our demand for Israel's withdrawal from
all occupied Lebanese territories. And
with regards to developments in the
Republic of Sudan, the Federal Republic
of Somalia, and the state of Libya, we
affirm the need to adhere to peaceful
resolution and to engage in political
dialogue to resolve disputes as per the
relevant security council resolutions
and the principles of international law
so as to protect the unity, territorial
integrity, and sovereignty of these
sisterly nations. Mr. Mr. President,
since Kuwait's independence, our foreign
policy was based on firm principles,
namely moderation and balance and a firm
commitment to the charter of the United
Nations and international law
and on support for multilateralism and
the belief that dialogue and the
peaceful settlement of disputes are the
best means to maintain international
peace and security. The state of Kuwait
also believes in a complimentary
relationship between security and
development. There can be no security
without development and no development
without security. Accordingly, Kuwait
has uh based its uh development and
humanitarian diplomacy
uh on a pioneering role for the Kuwait
Fund for Arab Economic Development.
Since 1961, the fund has contributed to
financing development projects in 107
countries. This stems from a belief that
addressing the root causes of crisis is
not limited to security measures, but
requires supporting development,
providing the foundations for a life of
dignity, and building more resilient and
stable societies. At the national level,
Kuwait is confidently progressing
towards its Kuwait vision 2035
by accelerating the implementation of
development projects, diversifying its
economy and sources of income,
continuing its digital transformation,
empowering women and youth, developing
its legislation, and consolidating
governance and transparency. These
efforts should enhance the efficiency of
institutions and the competitiveness of
the economy and will establish Kuwait as
a leading financial commercial and
control center in the region. In
conclusion, Mr. President, my country
has known the cruelty of occupation and
the bitterness of aggression and has
suffered from wars that have ravaged and
continue to ravage our region for four
decades. From this experience, we have
realized that they are the people who
pay the price of conflicts. We have
recognized the need for the world to
stand together united in support of
justice and in adherence to the UN
charter and international law. Out of
our experience, we became firmly
convinced that peace is the choice of
wisdom and is protected by ability and
dialogue does not diminish rights, but
preserves them. And that security is not
protected by force alone, but it is
anchored in justice, the rule of law,
and the principles of international
legitimacy. The message of the state of
Kuwait is one that has embraced in both
word and deed and to which it remains
committed that a just peace is the path
to stability and that respect for state
sovereignty, the preservation of the
rights of people and recourse to
international law for resolving disputes
are indispensable pillars for security
and stability of all states. The state
of Kuwait shall remain, as the world has
known it to be, a voice of wisdom and
moderation, a proponent of dialogue,
cooperation, and openness to
partnerships that serve mutual
interests, a champion of justice, and a
partner in consolidating international
peace and security. We believe that
peace is the path to a future where
rights are protected, nations are
stable, and generations enjoy security
and prosperity. And may the peace and
blessings of God be upon you.
On behalf of the assembly, I wish to
thank the crown prince of the state of
Kuwait.
